subject: general
question: In which year were Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added in the list of languages of the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2004.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
The **92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003**, which was published in the Gazette of India on January 8th, 2004, added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali to the list of languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India.

 
 
• 
 
The Constitution was initially translated into **14 different languages back in 2004.**

 
 
• 
 
There are now **22 languages included.**

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Oriya, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri are only some of the **22 languages in this group.**
 
• In **1967, support for Sindhi was implemented.**
 
• As of **1992, **support was added for Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali.
 
• An** additional four languages, **Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali, were included in 2004.
